scope: Pooled TP=4 synthetic staggered-workload benchmark receipts only.

aggregation.pooling: Concatenate every measured request from every repeat in one input report; warmup requests are excluded by the producer.
aggregation.output_tokens_per_s: sum(request.usage.completion_tokens for every pooled request) / total_wall_s; not the arithmetic mean of per-repeat throughput.
aggregation.nearest_rank_quantile: Sort all N pooled request values; select 1-based rank ceil(q*N), equivalently sorted_values[ceil(q*N)-1]. With N=16 and q=0.95, this selects rank 16 (the maximum), not the mean of repeat P95 values.
aggregation.ttft_s: Time from HTTP request start to the first nonempty text SSE event.
aggregation.tpot_s: (last_nonempty_text_SSE_time - first_nonempty_text_SSE_time) / (completion_tokens - 1); request-level average, not an individual token latency sample.
aggregation.slo_attainment: count(pooled requests satisfying joint_slo_met) / count(pooled requests)
aggregation.repeat_hash_stability: For each request index, compare text_sha256 across every measured repeat of that same input report.
aggregation.max_content_event_gap_s: Maximum reported gap between consecutive nonempty text SSE events across pooled requests; events are not guaranteed to map one-to-one to tokens.

producer.prompt_construction: For request index i and input length n: token[offset] = 100 + (i*97 + offset*31) % 20000, offset=0..n-1.

repeat_variation.interpretation: Observed per-repeat values are retained; no statistical-significance claim or attribution to a specific cause is made.

interpretation_limits: SSE event counts may be less than completion_tokens because the producer records only nonempty text events. This does not by itself demonstrate a dropped token or truncated response.
The producer raises before saving a report if a response lacks DONE, usage, nonempty text, or the requested completion-token count; raw HTTP frames are not retained in this summary.
Synthetic benchmark repeat hashes are separate evidence from natural-language correctness tests.
Hash consistency checks returned text bytes, not generated token IDs or model-state equivalence.
An unstable native repeat is not a single immutable output reference for cross-mode comparisons.
Goodput uses each input report benchmark SLO thresholds; the benchmark TTFT threshold and adaptive scheduler TTFT target may differ.
These are two-repeat descriptive measurements, not confidence intervals or production workload claims.

descriptive_comparison_to_native.interpretation: Adaptive fenced pooled throughput is about 0.6% above native in these two repeats, while pooled TTFT P95 is higher. This is a descriptive observation and does not establish a statistically significant speedup.
